patch_description: Replace the uniform reciprocal-link charge with a demand-weighted two-node cut estimate. Traffic leaving or entering a node pair must cross that pair’s boundary; reciprocal links reduce the available boundary links. A second-order expansion of inverse squared boundary capacity therefore gives a pairwise penalty that emphasizes cuts carrying more traffic. Centering the associated linear terms by endpoint effects preserves their ranking contribution across valid degree-two topologies, while reusing the existing reciprocal couplings keeps the QUBO compact.
